stances.reasoning: Co-sponsored Medicare for All (H.1239/S.744), a single-payer bill covering all MA residents with no premiums or co-pays.

Did not co-sponsor Sunlight Act or other transparency bills (all marked red X). However, Gomez stated he is a 'total proponent' of transparency and wants the public to understand how and why legislators vote. This rhetorical commitment without co-sponsorship aligns with a disclosure-focused position.

Co-sponsored Campaign Childcare (H.669/S.422) and has emphasized supporting vulnerable families in his district. His focus on equity and supporting those 'hurting the most' is consistent with expanding childcare subsidies.

Co-sponsored the CARE Act (Commission for Anti-Racism and Equity in Education). As the first Afro-Latino MA senator, Gomez has emphasized racial equity, police reform, and lived experience of communities of color as central to his legislative work.

Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act, preventing local enforcement from cooperating with ICE for civil immigration enforcement. Represents Springfield, a majority-minority city with a large immigrant population.

Co-sponsored Overdose Prevention Centers (H.1981/S.1242), a harm-reduction approach connecting people to housing and social services. His emphasis on equity and supporting struggling constituents is consistent with a services-first approach to homelessness.

Co-sponsored Lift the Ban on Local Tenant Protections, enabling municipalities to enact rent control and other tenant protections. Has described personally understanding what it means to be unable to pay rent as a renter himself.
Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act, preserving immigrant access to public safety and services regardless of immigration status.

Co-sponsored Age of Criminal Majority to 21, which would raise the age at which individuals are treated as adults in the criminal justice system, reducing incarceration of young people. Did not co-sponsor Prison Moratorium.
Co-sponsored the Safe Communities Act, ending state and local cooperation with ICE for civil immigration enforcement and prohibiting police from asking about immigration status.
Co-sponsored Medicare for All (H.1239/S.744), establishing a universal single-payer program for all MA residents regardless of age.
Co-sponsored the Cherish Act (Fully Funded Public Higher Ed), supporting full public education funding. Represents an underserved district where public school investment is critical.

Co-sponsored Stop Corporate Offshoring (H.2708/S.1925) and supports the millionaire's tax to fund housing and education. Has stated he wants to redirect marijuana industry revenue back to constituents for housing and education.
Did not co-sponsor Voting Rights Restoration (marked red X on Act on Mass tracker). No documented evidence of additional voting access positions.
